**Scope(s):** `THEORY-LEVEL` · **Row count:** 7 · **Lifecycle (candidate):** ACTIVE · **Layer (provisional):** LAYER-UNRESOLVED
**Notations:** `K_kernel=(K_t,B_t,Z_t,Q_t,delta_t)`, `Q_B(K_t,K_{t+1}) transformation-quality functional` · **Aliases:** `Chapter 16 combined with 10-15 quality-control reading`, `healthy vs pathological epistemic transformation`
**Candidate group membership (NOT an identity claim):**
- **G0505**: linked with `hpa-gita-chapter16-daivi-asuri-kernel-quality-model` — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'hpa-gita-chapter16-combined-quality-control-pathology-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter16-daivi-asuri-kernel-quality-model' (batch B0054). Note: A second, distinct hpa treatment of Chapter 16 combined with the full Chapters 10-15 model (companion to S2241, which read Ch16 alone): reframes daivi/asuri not as virtue/vice but as two classes of epistemic OPERATING BEHAVIOUR (healthy vs pathological transformation). Contributes a kernel pathology model distinguishing healthy (Evidence->Discrimination->Qualification->Knowledge) from distorted (Desire->Selection->Rationalization->False Knowledge) transformation pipelines; reframes Zero as the kernels ability to represent the boundary between knowledge and non-knowledge (false certainty = the kernel believing unknown=known, the near-opposite of Zero); introduces a transformation-quality functional Q_B(K_t,K_{t+1}); makes purification explicitly non-monotonic (a legitimate epistemic improvement can involve decreasing confidence); proposes an invariant against unjustified certainty (U(x)->C(x) requires sufficient justification); and reinforces Buddhi(discrimination) != Governance(legitimate constraint over action) as a restatement of Guidance!=Authority. Proposes final kernel tuple K_kernel=(K_t,B_t,Z_t,Q_t,delta_t).
- **G0506**: linked with `gita-refined-kernel-model-false-unknown-unqualified-triad` — explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'gita-refined-kernel-model-false-unknown-unqualified-triad' POSSIBLY relates to 'hpa-gita-chapter16-combined-quality-control-pathology-model' (batch B0054). Note: A deliberate model-refinement pause (explicitly before adding Chapter 17) consolidating the batch's Buddhi/Zero/Qualify/purification threads. Introduces the False != Unknown != Unqualified triad (p->R vs p->Z vs p->Q), refines Qualify to {Qualified,Unqualified,Undetermined,Terminus}, gives a restraint invariant Claim Strength <= Evidence Strength, a partition invariant set (Accepted(K) cap Rejected(K) = empty; Unknown(K) not-equiv Rejected(K); Unqualified(K) not-equiv Unknown(K)), a four-way kernel decomposition (primitives {Represent,Discriminate,Qualify,DetectGap,Transform}; state K_t; control properties {Restraint,Consistency,Provenance,Uncertainty}; external governance {Authority,Policy,Authorization,Action}), and a single central candidate kernel equation K_{t+1}=delta(Q(B(M(O_t,K_t))),K_t). Proposes a 12-question Kernel Algebra Research checklist including whether Buddhi is idempotent (B(B(x))=B(x)) and whether it can be non-monotonic under revision.
